name: Sissy Squat
description: The sissy squat is a unique quadriceps exercise in which the knees travel far forward of the toes while the torso leans backward, creating a long moment arm at the knee and intense quadriceps loading through a full range of motion. Unlike most squat variations, the hip does not flex significantly, making this primarily an open-chain knee extension pattern performed without a machine. It places high eccentric stress on the quadriceps and substantial load on the patellar tendon.

execution.starting_position: Stand with heels slightly elevated (on a small plate or the edge of a step) and hold onto an upright support for balance. Feet are hip-width apart.
execution.setup_instructions: Have a fixed support nearby (rack upright or door frame) to hold during the movement. Heel elevation (1–2 inches) makes the exercise more accessible and reduces ankle mobility demands.
steps: Step 1: Stand tall, holding the support lightly for balance. Begin to lean backward as a unit from the knees — the ankle plantar-flexes and the knee flexes.
Step 2: Continue leaning backward while allowing the knees to travel far forward. The hips remain relatively extended throughout — do not flex at the hip.
Step 3: Descend until the thighs are as close to vertical as possible (nearly parallel to the torso, which is leaning far back).
Step 4: Reverse the motion by contracting the quadriceps powerfully to pull the torso back to vertical.
Step 5: Return to full standing extension.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale during the descent. Exhale on the return to standing.
common_mistakes: Hinging at the hip (like a squat) instead of maintaining hip extension throughout
Moving too fast through the eccentric portion — the sissy squat's value is in its slow, controlled range
Attempting without sufficient quad strength — high patellar tendon stress makes unpreparedness risky
safety_considerations: High patellar tendon load — those with patellar tendinopathy should consult a clinician before performing
Avoid the loaded version until bodyweight is controlled comfortably
Heel elevation reduces the ankle dorsiflexion requirement and reduces risk of balance loss
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Maximize the backward lean while keeping hips extended and feet planted. The more range, the greater the quad stretch.
coaching_cues: Keep the hips long — do not fold at the hip
Lean back as one rigid plank from knee to shoulder
Squeeze the quads to pull yourself back up
